who-this-is-for.text: As a name controller, I want wallet change to leave recovery and retirement available. This specification follows issue 146 and the frozen operator acceptance of September fifteenth.

required-behavior.text: Maintenance and recovery preserve exactly the non-ADA policies, names and quantities, allowing ADA top-up. An added token refuses as record value preservation. Insert fold creates only the representative and ADA. The diagram shows these preservation steps and the refusal branch before a polluted continuation becomes a record.

existing-polluted-records.text: The three reproductions become permanent tests. Polluted recovery and retirement return a named Boolean refusal instead of crashing. Unchanged polluted maintenance remains accepted. This does not repair an old record or migrate an old script output.

acceptance-and-controls.text: Boolean refusal tests must fail on a crash. Clean controls accept. Added, removed, replaced and increased tokens refuse, while ADA top-up accepts. Recovery and insert-fold pollution also refuse. A compiled cage test checks names, the suites and CI pass, identity is regenerated, and Haskell readers inspect the complete value.

model-binding-and-limits.text: Lean stays at the exact bound repository revision. Its output contains one representative, quantity and scalar value. Naming lifecycle transitions remain authoritative. Multi-asset encoding is the operator-assigned implementation refinement; the correspondence names its enforcement. Fixtures prove component behavior only. No preprod deployment.
